A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dataset and foundation-model project, renamed from Surg-3M/SurgFM to LEMON/LemonFM. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial evaluation and presentation revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original downstream evaluations, model ablations, data-scaling experiments, video-classification results, and cross-validation results for its curation models.

after.justification: v3 reports original linear-probing and fine-tuning evaluations, semantic-segmentation results, curation and architecture ablations, and retained video-classification and curation-model results.

M1.justification: The ConvNeXt-L teacher/student architecture, augmented-distillation loss and sampling, temporal phase head, and typicality-weighted video classifier remain substantially unchanged. v3 adds an FPN decoder adaptation for semantic segmentation. The YOLOv8 preprocessing described under curation was already present in v2 Section 4 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: v3 adds CholecSeg8k semantic segmentation, introducing pixel-wise prediction as a fourth downstream task. It removes SAR-RARP50 action recognition and GraSP phase recognition, while retaining GraSP tool detection. The underlying 4,194-video, 35-procedure pretraining dataset and its two video-classification tasks remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds Endo-FM, GSViT, and SurgeNetXL to evaluated downstream comparisons and substantially revises comparator membership on retained tasks. Removed comparators include Ramesh et al., SSL4EVA, several phase specialists, Tripnet/Attention Tripnet, and TAPIS for GraSP tool detection. The Table 6 video-classification comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes the stated downstream resolution from 448×448 to 224×224 and specifies a separate linear-probing protocol using batch size 512 and learning rate 1e-3. CholecT50 reporting changes from video-level to frame-level mAP, while its explicit five-fold split description is replaced by a different protocol citation. Segmentation introduces an FPN decoder, mDice, and a 75%/25% video split. These are reported protocol revisions, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 replaces v2's Cholec80/CholecT50 design ablations with AutoLaparo/CholecSeg8k analyses, adding curated-versus-raw pretraining and a ConvNeXt-B size control. Backbone and augmented-distillation effects are tested under the new settings, while the explicit DINO/DINOv2 comparison disappears. The 10%/25% data-scaling analyses are removed; 50% evaluations remain.

E5.justification: v3 removes the ± uncertainty reporting from the main ablation, phase-recognition, and action-recognition tables, together with the data-scaling variability plot. Five-fold curation statistics and the stated five-fold evaluation at 50% training data remain. v3 newly specifies random seed 30 for pretraining and downstream training; this does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive foundation-model comparison and ablation results, including 81.3 mDice versus EndoViT's 73.0 on CholecSeg8k. Reported AutoLaparo accuracy changes from 85.2 to 85.5, and CholecT50 mAP from 64.2 to 61.9; revised settings prevent interpreting these as matched performance gains or losses. Results for removed tasks disappear, whereas the video-classification leaderboard and curation-model statistics are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1 and 2 retain the augmented-distillation objective and typicality-weighted video aggregation, including their mathematical definitions and parameters. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 introduces no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The main performance claim shifts from specialist-focused success on three tasks to superiority over surgical foundation models across four tasks, explicitly including semantic segmentation. Low-data claims are recast around outperforming foundation-model comparators with 50% labeled data, replacing v2's additional claims involving 10%. The underlying dataset, curation, and foundation-model contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 develops an empirical argument for rigorous curation and broadens its interpretation of SSL results to discriminative objectives versus generative objectives. It removes v2's discussion of sparse-data degradation on GraSP and online-versus-offline qualifications. The conclusion replaces pixel-wise adaptation and self-distillation limitations with future work on a surgical video foundation model.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents Ubuntu, PyTorch/CUDA versions, downstream CPU/A100 hardware, and the teacher's exponential-moving-average update. Appendix F specifies that direct LMDB access covers the 1-fps dataset version, where v2 called it the full dataset. Most pretraining hyperparameters, curation annotations, licensing instructions, and video-classification split details are retained.

R1.justification: Dataset positioning shifts from an 18-fold size comparison with Cholec80 to explicit comparisons with GenSurgery and SurgeNetXL, emphasizing curation quality and procedure coverage through Table 1 and Figure 3. References for these projects and segmentation are added, while works associated with removed evaluations disappear. This substantially revises the competitive context beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming, v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, contributions, experimental discussion, and conclusion. Evaluation and results are consolidated into Section 5, task annotations gain a separate subsection, preprocessing moves into dataset curation, and Appendix D is reorganized around splits, linear probing, and full fine-tuning.

P2.justification: v3 reorganizes task-specific result tables into cross-task linear-probing and fine-tuning tables, adds a segmentation table and dataset-comparison figure, and redraws the radar and pipeline diagrams. The procedure-diversity figure moves to the supplement, the data-scaling plot disappears, and ablation and leaderboard displays are redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports the central foundation-model and dataset-quality claims through direct surgical-foundation-model comparisons, a curated-versus-raw ablation, and segmentation experiments addressing v2's explicit pixel-wise limitation. These gains are tempered by lost downstream uncertainty reporting, reduced low-data and task coverage, and removed specialist comparisons, including TAPIS on retained GraSP tool detection. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than an unqualified substantial gain.
